chapter: The 1949 band, breakup and later years
title: Willie Smith's last work and the end of his band business
summary: Willie Smith's final recordings and film were with Barnet, who considers Las Vegas the end of his band business.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: So actually, Pat, that was -- oh then I had an engagement in Las Vegas after that, which I'd already signed, and there again I was going to take Willy up, but I was going to put together a Las Vegas band. Unfortunately, Willy passed away.
So Willy's last work was with you.
And the last time he would have been on film was that film made in New York.
And the last recordings would have been those transcriptions you made, right?

The transcriptions, the sound track, and also the album we made in Hollywood before we went east. They were all with me. I did the Las Vegas thing, and well, that was that. As far as I'm concerned that was the end of me in the band business. I've done a few other things since then. I put a band together and played Disneyland, and -- it was a hell of a band. Of course I spent more money on the band than I got because I rehearsed for five days to play two nights, and paid the guys for rehearsal, because I wanted it to be good.
